title: Mount shared views and couple capture to displayed state

title: Define joint artifact and view-state contract
description: Specify and implement the versioned boundary that lets Canvas, a human, and an agent refer to the same visual thing and the same exact view of it. Cover finite artifacts and live sources without coupling the document to SSE, inbox, filesystem, camera, or model-provider details.
design: Model source identity/provenance separately from ViewState. A view owns normalized viewport, optional selection/annotation, page or playhead, filters and source revision. All mutations use optimistic revisions. Capture/inspection must name the resulting view revision so an agent cannot silently inspect pixels different from what Canvas shows.
acceptance_criteria: Rust types validate source references, provenance and bounded shared view state; patches can focus a normalized image region without replacing the artifact; serialization is MCP-schema-compatible; tests cover invalid bounds, stale revisions and a finite image plus a live graph source; the architecture document gives a manual runbook from source resolution to shared display and inspection.
notes: Implemented dock_canvas::view contract with keyed multi-source bindings, artifact/live source positions, normalized viewport, visible attention ownership, page/timeline navigation, typed parameters, and atomic revision-checked patches. Tests prove image-region focus preserves artifact identity, two live sources share one view lifecycle, invalid regions/source modes fail, stale patches conflict, and JSON round-trips. Added architecture boundary and manual runbook; repaired existing all-feature mlua callback/table integration exposed by the gate.
close_reason: The shared multi-source artifact/view-state contract, validation, patch semantics, tests, architecture document, and runbook are implemented.

title: Make Canvas the shared human-agent visualization plane
description: Canvas is the common visualization layer for static artifacts and live data, and the joint visual context shared by a human and AI. Any authorized source can publish typed data or references; deterministic reducers and capability-scoped Lua map them into views; both parties observe and change the same revisioned view state instead of maintaining separate chat and screen representations.
design: Separate immutable or owner-referenced artifacts from mutable joint view state. Normalize finite snapshots and unbounded streams behind one typed source contract. Keep transport, authorization, decoding and rendering outside Lua; Lua adapts bounded typed inputs into retained visual scenes. MCP expresses intent and reads exact state; the owner-local socket applies deterministic revisioned transitions. View state includes viewport, selection, page/playhead, filters, presentation and provenance so agent inspection is visibly mirrored on Canvas.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can publish or resolve an artifact/data source, open a shared view, focus or annotate the exact region it is inspecting, and capture that same view revision; human interactions update the state the agent reads; one streaming source and one finite artifact use the same lifecycle; a Lua adapter can render a bounded unfamiliar graph stream without owning I/O; provenance and authorization remain inspectable.
notes: 2026-09-08 product direction: Canvas is the shared view/window manager for human-AI collaboration and the common view language for all signals. Reference workloads include Elmer's brain and MCP firing SSE graphs, Edgerunner DAGs, Prometheus instruments, Panopticon maps, trading/mixed-export analysis, presence, terminals/NVR/media, STL/STEP/wireframe/FEA/CAM/microscope, Gaussian splats/RuView/PolyLayout, music visualizers, generated CSV+Lua/template explanations, Maxim-style narratives and future XR. Preserve steering/observability and hands-on engineering/vibe-coding as equal modes. Alfalfa owns identity/workflow/admin; JARVIS owns voice/presence; domain systems own data/actions/hardware; Canvas owns shared views/layout/capture/presentation. Portable state uses compact JSON snapshots plus JSONL patch/receipt journals; Lua owns bounded presentation logic.

title: Configure Canvas overlays and global visibility

title: Present Canvas as one shared desktop across displays
description: A single oversized native Canvas window records a multi-display frame but macOS separate Spaces prevents reliable presentation across the physical displays. Present one host window per selected display while retaining one WorkspaceDocument, one global z-order, and one virtual coordinate space so surfaces can be dragged across seams.
design: Add a renderer-neutral display topology and virtual-to-local projection boundary. The shell owns one borderless window per display and renders/clips the shared document through each display viewport. Pointer events translate from host-window local coordinates into virtual desktop coordinates before using the existing interaction engine. Monitor assignment remains host-local and socket/MCP driven.
acceptance_criteria: On the current three-display Mac, Canvas visibly covers each selected display; a surface can be dragged across both seams while preserving size, focus, and z-order; disconnect/reconnect and nonzero/negative origins fail or reconcile deterministically; socket inspection exposes selected display targets; tests cover topology, projection, and cross-display pointer translation.
notes: 2026-09-08 shared desktop slice implemented: one native host window per selected display over one WorkspaceDocument/global z-order/virtual frame; window-local pointer coordinates project to shared coordinates; display target exposed through socket and Canvas MCP; tests cover negative origins, seam projection, topology validation and second-display pointer translation. Live three-display 5760x1200 presentation verified by user and visibility hotkey proof. Remaining before closing: respond to display topology changes at runtime and prove disconnect/reconnect reconciliation without restarting Canvas.

Focus is then a no-op because App.window remains unset. Closing or relaunching must recreate the desktop presentation instead of leaving a headless control process.

title: Stop Canvas background flicker and expose frame pacing
description: The animated Canvas background flickers severely in the live desktop. Make shader animation opt-in while unstable, schedule generation at a bounded cadence, measure generated/presented cadence over a rolling interval, and expose a small configurable FPS diagnostic so frame pacing can be verified before deployment.
design: Keep timing deterministic in the Canvas runtime. Separate tick cadence, expensive shader generation cadence, and diagnostic sampling. Do not perform synchronous GPU readback unless animated background state explicitly enables it.
acceptance_criteria: The default Canvas launch is visually stable. Shader frames are never generated faster than the configured cap. A socket-controlled FPS overlay reports measured cadence. Tests cover disabled/default scheduling, capped scheduling, and meter calculation. The live right-monitor instance is verified without flicker.

title: Render Panopticon intelligence as a native Canvas map
description: Add a first-class renderer-neutral map surface and native Canvas adapter. Canvas owns camera state, map interaction, transition timing, reduced-motion behavior, and compositing; it consumes authorized opaque map resources and never stores credentials or asks Panopticon to dictate pixels. Resolve natural-language place names outside the renderer into exact versioned geographic extents, then apply deterministic camera intents. Use a proven map engine through an offscreen texture boundary rather than implementing tile layout, labels, collision, and camera flight from scratch.
design: Define maps.viewport.v1 with target variants extent, center_zoom, entity, and current_results; WGS84 antimeridian-safe bounds; padding; bearing/pitch; and a renderer hint transition of jump, ease, or fly with bounded duration. Derive center/zoom from extent plus actual surface size instead of storing redundant values. Add a Map surface/resource binding to the WorkspaceDocument and revisioned patch protocol. Prototype MapLibre Native FFI owned-texture or borrowed-texture compositing on macOS Metal, keeping network/tile parsing off the iced render thread. The MCP path accepts an already-resolved extent or stable place reference; an orchestrator may resolve a phrase through Panopticon before issuing one exact Canvas mutation. Ambiguity must return candidates, never silently choose Springfield/Fremont. Preserve human gestures and cancel/retarget an in-flight agent animation deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: From one MCP-driven request, Canvas can show and smoothly fly between world, Seattle, Fremont Seattle, Manhattan, the five boroughs, and the NY/NJ/CT tri-state extent; fit current query results; and follow an entity. Camera movement is smooth on reference hardware, interruptible by direct human input, honors reduced motion, and does not mutate the durable document every frame. Retina output is sharp, labels do not visibly reflow after settling, stale tile/data failures are explicit, and credentials/endpoints never appear in the document or MCP receipt. Unit tests cover extent fitting, antimeridian bounds, ambiguity, revision conflicts, duration bounds, and transition cancellation; a live visual test records frame-time and command-to-first-motion latency.
notes:
Backend-first slice implemented locally without selecting a permanent engine: added a generic typed VisualBackend lifecycle with shared mount/update/resize/input/event/render/suspend/unmount semantics, revision enforcement, reduced-motion context, retained-frame outcomes, and adapter-neutral errors. Added maps.viewport model types with opaque resource identity, semantic layers, extent/center/follow/fit targets, antimeridian-safe bounds, provenance refs, surface-derived Web Mercator camera fitting, bounded jump/ease/fly transitions, and reduced-motion resolution. Validation on 2026-09-07 used /Volumes/DOC MOVIES/dock-cargo-target because the local disk filled: all 48 dock-canvas all-feature library tests pass and strict all-feature library Clippy with -D warnings passes. Focused rustfmt is clean. Concurrent Canvas work remains in the shared worktree and was preserved. Remaining on this feature: put MapSurface into the WorkspaceDocument after current document work settles, implement the MapLibre FFI texture adapter behind VisualBackend, wire map gestures/animation interruption, add map-specific MCP convenience operations, and perform native visual/performance proof.
2026-09-07 renderer direction: native-first Rust + Lua + wgpu/WGSL. Do not introduce deck.gl or a large JavaScript visualization runtime. MapLibre Native may remain a bounded C++/FFI map backend behind VisualBackend; Canvas owns the Rust compositor and MCP surface. Treat browser rendering as a thin fallback or a build from the shared typed scene contract, not the source of truth.
Wishlist extension from the operational-view audit: native map presentation should also compose trip-planning views for sailing and camping—route, waypoints, scale/bearing, weather, tides/currents, hazards and contact cards—while Panopticon and other source connectors retain ownership of geography, query and trip data.

title: Add direct mouse interaction and drag placement to Canvas
description: Build the renderer-neutral Canvas interaction engine needed for immediate direct manipulation: hit testing, pointer capture, click-to-focus, drag-to-move, resize handles, z-order promotion, and predictable edge/grid snapping. The iced shell will translate native mouse events into this engine and apply validated workspace patches so agents and humans share the same placement model.

The engine returns deterministic intents; the authoritative workspace/runtime validates and applies them. No OS mouse injection or Accessibility permission belongs here.

title: Canvas: split into a backend with the cache and presence-routed dumb screens
notes:
Prerequisite for dock-fwd (MCP-mediated retrieval). Routing every agent's document reads through one process on one Mac couples all agents to that machine and drags their data across the network to reach a screen. Agents should stay fast with their data nearby; screens should be observers.

Shape:
- A backend owns the content cache and the canonical state, and lives near the
  agents rather than near the screens.
- Canvas instances subscribe. They render and interact; they do not own truth.
- JARVIS presence routes: content flows to screens someone is actually at.

The distinction that makes this work is two planes with different economics:

CONTROL PLANE - what exists, what changed, statuses, which document an agent
just opened. Small, cheap, always flowing regardless of observers. This is the
'state should still update' requirement, and it is what lets a screen know what
it WOULD need before anyone arrives.

DATA PLANE - rasterized pages, crops, images, frames. Large, expensive, and only
worth moving to an observed screen. This is what presence gates.

Conflating them gives you a system that is either wasteful (streaming pixels to
empty rooms) or stale (nothing updates until someone walks up). Splitting them
gives both.

Consequences worth designing for:

1. Content addressing makes the cache distributable for free. media.rs already
   keys by sha256 (MediaCacheKey) and main.rs keeps background_assets in a
   sha256 map, so a screen can ask 'do I have abc123' locally before pulling,
   caches can sit anywhere without a coherence protocol, and regenerating the
   same crop twice costs nothing.

2. Presence enables prefetch, not just suppression. With the control plane
   current, a screen knows what it would need before anyone arrives, so
   detecting approach can warm the data plane rather than leaving a wall blank
   for two seconds. Anticipation is the more interesting use of presence than
   saving bandwidth.

3. A screen must survive an unreachable backend. Canvas today is authoritative -
   it owns workspaces.json, the document and reconcile.rs - so inverting that
   makes a partition into a dead wall unless local last-known state is retained
   and marked stale. That is docs/widget-quality.md rule 2 at the system layer:
   a screen showing old state must say it is old rather than looking live.

4. Where truth lives is a tenet-4 one-way door. Decide once whether the backend
   is authoritative for workspace documents or only for content, because
   reconcile.rs's whole design assumes a local authoritative document.

Open: one backend per site or one per agent host; how a screen authenticates to
it (the bridge already brokers authenticated egress, see metric_reads); and
whether the existing stream.sock contract extends across a network or is
strictly the last local hop.
BUFFERING AND REPLAY: a backend gives the stream a retained position, and the client contract for it already exists.

crates/canvas/src/view.rs:47-51 defines SourcePosition { Live { observed_sequence }, Sequence { sequence } }, documented as 'hold a live source at an exact replayable sequence', and every view source carries one (config/views/fleet-runtime.json has position.kind live with observed_sequence 0).

Nothing serves it. stream.sock is fire-and-forget UnixDatagram with no retention, so a screen that misses events has no way to catch up and observed_sequence is decorative. A backend that retains a bounded window per stream makes it real, and gives:
- a reconnecting screen catching up rather than showing a gap
- a screen that was asleep or unobserved rewinding when someone arrives, which
  is what makes presence-gated data flow safe rather than lossy
- deterministic replay for a shared link, which needs a sequence rather than
  whatever happens to arrive after it opens

Retention is bounded by the same logic as everything else here: enough to cover
a reconnect and a presence gap, not an archive.

title: Canvas: route document retrieval through MCP so Canvas sees it first
notes:
When an agent reads a document, Canvas should see it before the agent does. Displaying then stops being something the agent must remember and becomes inherent in how reading works - the same principle as dock-tiz: the tool carries the invariant, not the agent's context.

Why this is the highest-leverage of the firehose ideas:

1. It makes the right path the easy path. A typed MCP call is far easier to emit
   correctly than a bash incantation, especially for smaller models, so agents
   adopt it because it is less work rather than because a rule says so.
   Enforcement mostly takes care of itself once the good path is cheaper.
2. It is cheaper in tokens. Returning page 4 cropped to a region costs a
   fraction of catting a PDF into context, so the agent gets faster answers and
   the human gets a view, from the same call.
3. It gives cropping a natural home. media.rs today has
   MediaVariant::PdfPage { page_index } (media.rs:61) with rasterization,
   MediaPlan and a resize-invalidating cache, but no region. A
   MediaVariant::PdfRegion { page_index, rect } serves the agent asking for a
   section and the human seeing exactly that section, from one plan.

Existing surface to build on: OpenFile is already both a control command
(control.rs:63, 1317) and an MCP tool (mcp.rs:74). What is missing is that
retrieval returns content to the agent AND places it, rather than doing one or
the other.

Design notes:
- Placement should follow dock-8cd: a surface per document, spatially stable,
  bounded working set, so retrieval does not strobe the wall.
- Sensitivity applies. What an agent reads is among the most revealing things
  on a screen, so this must respect dock-7pa presence gating.
- 'Enforce' is the wrong lever. Make the MCP path better - crop, pagination,
  no context blowup - and the bash path withers on its own.
BLOCKED ON dock-qwv (backend + presence-routed screens).

Building this first would couple every agent to one process on one Mac and pull their data across the network to reach a screen. The retrieval path should be defined against the backend that owns the cache, not against a local Canvas, or it will need rewriting the moment a second machine runs agents.

The control/data plane split from dock-qwv also changes this design: an agent's retrieval publishes to the control plane always (what was opened, which region), and the rasterized crop moves on the data plane only to screens someone is at. Getting that boundary right is the difference between retrieval that scales to a fleet and retrieval that works on one desk.

title: Canvas control: make the protocol safe for agents by default
notes:
An agent drove the live workspace tonight and reported success while the human saw nothing. Nothing it did was against the rules; the protocol simply had no way to express them. The fix belongs in the interface, not in agent instructions - anything an agent must remember will be forgotten by an agent with a full context window.

What actually happened:
- 'view fleet/runtime' switched the active project from dock to bifrost. The
  command type is OpenOperationalView { view_id } (control.rs:134) and does not
  mention a project at all, yet switching one is its largest effect.
- 'shader 7' applied to whatever project happened to be active, which was not
  the one the human was looking at. Backgrounds are pinned per project, so it
  was invisible and then overwritten by dock's pinned aurora-drift.
- Every reply was 'OK rev=N'. The agent reported 'you should see fire now' on
  the strength of an acknowledgement, which is not an outcome.
- The project changed back between two inspects seconds apart, with no command
  from the agent. There is no attribution, so who did it is unanswerable.

Proposed, cheapest first:

1. Receipts describe what a viewer would now see, not that a command parsed.
   'OK rev=2189 shader=7' becomes 'OK project=dock displays=3 visible=true
   background=flame (was aurora-drift)'. Tonight this alone would have caught
   the mistake on the first command, because the reply would have said
   project=bifrost. Cheap: the DocumentSnapshot receipt (control.rs:1389)
   already carries most of these fields; mutations just do not return it.

2. Actor attribution. Every mutation records who issued it; inspect reports
   recent actors. 'The project changed and it was not me' becomes answerable
   rather than a mystery, and two agents fighting over one socket becomes
   visible instead of confusing. Cheap.

3. No implicit 'current' for mutations. A mutating command names its target or
   is rejected: shader 7 --project dock. This removes the entire class of bug
   where the target changes between read and write, and it makes an agent state
   its intent rather than inherit whatever is on screen. Medium: a protocol
   change, so it wants a version bump and a deprecation path.

4. Declare side effects in the command type. OpenOperationalView switching the
   project should be visible in its signature - either a project parameter the
   caller must supply, or a name that admits what it does. Tenet 4: a good
   interface is hard to misuse. Medium.

5. Human-presence guard, the actual sane default. If a human has interacted
   recently, an agent mutation to their ACTIVE project requires an explicit
   override or is routed to a scratch project. This is lockout's shape applied
   to the workspace instead of the CPU: a lease, with conflicts visible. It
   composes with dock-7pa, which already needs presence to distinguish the
   owner from anyone else. Largest, and the one that would make the default
   behaviour correct without the agent knowing anything.

6. Scratch project by default for unidentified clients, like a worktree for the
   desktop. An agent that does not name a target gets somewhere harmless.
   Pairs with 3.

7. --dry-run returning the receipt without applying, so an agent can check what
   a command would change before changing it. Cheap once 1 exists.

1, 2 and 7 are worth doing immediately and are close to free. 5 is the one that
turns 'the agent behaved well' into 'the agent could not have misbehaved'.
REFRAME: infer and repair, not refuse. Rejecting a command makes the agent's job harder; inferring makes the tool's job harder, which is where the difficulty belongs.

The seam already exists. crates/canvas/src/reconcile.rs is a declarative reconciler - DesiredWorkspaceState in, NoChange | ApplyPatch | ApplyDocument out, with ReconcileMode { Preserve, Exact } already expressing repair-toward-desired.

What is missing is the layer IN FRONT of it. reconcile.rs says so itself: 'Callers resolve natural language, project identity, and authorized resources before constructing DesiredWorkspaceState.' Resolution is pushed onto the caller and nothing validates the result. Tonight the caller resolved 'which project' wrong and the system had no opinion.

So the work is a resolver, not a gate:

1. Imperative control commands become sugar. 'shader 7', 'view X', 'bg Y' compile
   into a DesiredWorkspaceState and go through reconcile like everything else,
   instead of poking state directly. One path, one set of invariants.

2. Target resolution infers from observable signals rather than an internal
   cursor. The default target is the project on the display the human is
   actually present at - presence already distinguishes Verified from Detected
   (control.rs:362). 'The active project' is an implementation detail; 'what the
   human is looking at' is the intent, and it is knowable.

3. Repair rather than reject. If a desired state would land somewhere invisible,
   route it to the visible surface and say so, rather than erroring. An agent
   asking for Flame wants to see Flame; applying it to an off-screen project is
   technically obedient and practically useless.

4. The receipt reports what was inferred, not just what was applied:
   'shader=flame project=dock (inferred from presence; bifrost was active but
   not visible)'. That is what makes an inferring system trustworthy - it shows
   its reasoning, so a wrong inference is visible instead of silent.

5. A ReconcileMode variant for this - Intent - which resolves underspecified
   fields from context instead of preserving or exacting them.

The through-line: the tool should be able to answer 'what did they mean' using
things it can observe - who is present, which display is lit, what was touched
last - rather than requiring the caller to have carried that context correctly.

title: Materialize authorized project resources into content-addressed local assets
description: Close the gap between Alfalfa owning the artifact map and Canvas being able to draw it. Alfalfa already owns resource identity -- project scopes carry resources[] as {id, kind, title, uri} with kinds like repo, note and tracker -- and the dock-workspaces MCP states outright that 'Alfalfa owns project and resource identity; Dock presents resources and never returns credentials or private source context.' What does not exist is the step in between: turning a resource_id into local bytes plus an AssetRef that Canvas can render.
design:
Canvas is deliberately unable to fetch. AssetRef{sha256, media_type, byte_length} carries NO URL: Canvas opens a local path, hashes it, and the AssetRef becomes the content identity. prune_decoded keys the decode cache on asset.sha256 and media.rs already has MediaCacheKey/MediaPlan/MediaLimits, so DECODED output is cached today -- but there is no store for source bytes and no network path anywhere in the crate. Keep it that way. NON-GOAL: Canvas gaining a fetch path. A saved workspace that referenced URLs would rot when they change, and a renderer that fetches is a renderer that can be pointed at anything.
Shape: a local resolver process, the same pattern as the stream relay for SSE. It holds credentials, resolves an Alfalfa resource_id (or a research-wing paper ID) outward, writes bytes into a content-addressed store, and hands back an AssetRef. Content addressing does the caching for free -- immutable, deduplicated across projects, and safe to share between surfaces -- and it composes with the existing sha256-keyed decode cache rather than duplicating it.
PROVENANCE RULE, which decides what is stored at all: can this artifact be regenerated deterministically? Generated PDFs (doc-forge dealer packets, invoices) are rebuildable from source plus template, so they are rebuilt and cached by hash, never committed. Third-party PDFs such as research papers cannot be regenerated -- they ARE the source -- and research-wing already owns immutable source revisions and exact preservation, so those resolve to a research-wing ID and a loading path rather than a second copy. The dividing line is provenance, not file type.
acceptance_criteria: A resource_id resolves to an AssetRef that Canvas renders, with no network call made by Canvas itself. Repeat resolution of unchanged content is a cache hit and refetches nothing. An unknown or unauthorized resource fails visibly, naming the resource, rather than rendering an empty surface. Credentials never appear in the workspace document, the asset store, or anything Canvas reads. Papers resolve through research-wing identity rather than being copied into a second store.
notes: Raised 2026-09-09 while auditing Canvas data paths. Sits alongside dock-cov.3.2 (contract registry) and dock-cov.3.3 (path classification): .3.3 classifies which sources need which path, this one builds the asset-path plumbing for the ones that need bytes on disk. Shares its shape with the SSE relay under discussion for Alfalfa executive summaries -- one local-relay pattern, two consumers -- so they are worth designing together rather than growing two credential-holding processes with different conventions. Open questions deliberately left for implementation: whether the source-byte store shares a root with the decode cache or stays separate, and what eviction looks like given that content addressing makes staleness impossible but unbounded growth easy.

title: Classify candidate Canvas data sources by ingestion path
description: Decide, per candidate source, which of Canvas's three existing ingestion paths it belongs to, before any of them are built. The paths differ by orders of magnitude in cost, so an undifferentiated wish list reads as one project when it is really several plus a pile of afternoons.
design:
Canvas already has three distinct paths and every candidate belongs to exactly one.
(1) BINDING PATH -- StreamEnvelope -> binders/<adapter>.lua -> widget snapshot -> InputPort. For small, structured, frequently updating numeric or text data. Near-free to add: a .lua file, no rebuild. The binder receives an already-decoded envelope and returns a snapshot; it is not a decode path and must not become one, and Lua cannot perform I/O.
(2) ASSET PATH -- AssetRef{sha256, media_type, byte_length} -> SurfaceContent::Asset or NodeContent::Image/Mesh. Content-addressed, fetched once, rendered natively.
(3) NATIVE SURFACE PATH -- continuous decode or GPU residency. SurfaceContent::Stream{url}, SurfaceContent::Terminal{resource_id} and SurfaceContent::Scene already exist as variants, but each source here is a rendering feature with frame pacing, backpressure and GPU lifetime concerns.
First-pass classification of the candidates raised 2026-09-09: binding path -- RSS, Prometheus (largely done under dock-cov.3.1.1), financial/OHLCV (market-ohlcv-v1 exists), SSE from Alfalfa/Elmers/MCP-Bridge, bounded text. Asset path -- images, PDFs, renderings, static meshes. Native surface path -- video/NVR, sound, FEA/CFD, Panopticon geospatial, terminal.
Remote sources do not connect directly: ingress is an owner-only Unix socket by design. A remote feed needs a local relay that authenticates outward and pushes inward, which keeps credentials in the relay and out of Canvas. One relay pattern serves RSS, SSE and financial feeds alike, so building it once is the unlock for most of path 1.
acceptance_criteria: Every candidate source is assigned a path with a stated reason. Path-3 candidates carry a named cost -- decoder, GPU residency, backpressure strategy -- rather than a bare title. The output sequences work: path-1 sources become individual small tasks, path-3 sources become their own beads sized as features. Sources already covered by existing work are marked as such rather than re-filed.
notes:
Raised by the owner 2026-09-09 asking whether to audit FPL systems for what should connect to Canvas. The useful audit is by path, not by source: path 1 is a .lua file and an afternoon, path 3 is a quarter of work each, and a flat list hides that difference. Also worth settling in the same pass: whether SurfaceContent::Stream{url} and Terminal{resource_id} are implemented or only declared, since three of the path-3 candidates depend on them.
First pass done by reading the renderer 2026-09-09. Which paths actually exist today, rather than which variants are declared:
REAL AND DEVELOPED. Binding path: stream.sock ingress, apply_named_adapter loading binders/<adapter>.lua, two binders on disk. Asset path: media.rs is 533 lines of real still-media machinery -- MediaLimits, MediaCacheKey with a stable cache key, MediaPlan, PDF rasterization and ResizeInvalidation. Images and PDFs are genuinely supported today. Terminal: implemented on its own PTY path in terminal.rs (spawn_terminal/read_fd/write_fd/kill_pid/close_fd), not through the decode pipeline, and constructed in reconcile.rs -- so terminal surfaces are real. Scene, Chart and Widget all dispatch in ensure_scene_decoded.
DECLARED ONLY. SurfaceContent::Stream{url} has exactly one construction site (main.rs:7806) and no decoder anywhere: no ffmpeg, rtsp or hls in the tree, and media.rs is still-image and PDF work, not continuous video. So video/NVR is the largest genuine gap on the candidate list -- a real feature with frame pacing, GPU residency and backpressure, not glue. Nothing found for audio at all.
WORTH NOTING. ensure_scene_decoded ends in '_ => continue', and SurfaceContent::Unsupported(_) renders a markdown tile naming what is missing rather than an empty rectangle. That is a good pattern and means an unimplemented source degrades legibly instead of silently -- new path-3 work should keep landing in it until it is real.
OPEN QUESTION that changes the classification: map.v1 already exists as a contract literal. If Panopticon can emit bounded map data rather than raster tiles, geospatial is binding path (cheap) rather than native surface (expensive). Worth settling before sizing it -- it may be the difference between an afternoon and a quarter.
ALSO: SurfaceContent::Unsupported exists in the Rust but is absent from the published MCP JSON schema, which lists only project_resource, asset, chart, widget, scene, terminal and stream. Agents therefore cannot express or expect it. Probably harmless, possibly a schema drift worth checking against dock-cov.3.2.
2026-09-09, from the widget-side audit (docs/widget-quality.md): the Real vs Declared-only axis has a second dimension worth separating.

crates/canvas/src/main.rs:3822 renders ContentSource::Stream { url } as 'Connecting to stream...' plus the URL. No decoder exists, so it never connects, but the surface asserts an in-progress connection indefinitely. That is not a neutral stub: it actively claims something false, and it claims it in the state a viewer is least likely to question.

Three instances of one pattern now:
- canvas-widgets/src/live.rs:22 mock_price() renders hashed values as quotes
- prometheus widgets sat on Loading before canvas-metrics existed, because
  nothing was ever going to emit a snapshot
- ContentSource::Stream renders Connecting forever

Note what this means for SurfaceContent::Unsupported: it catches UNKNOWN variants - 'this build cannot draw that kind' - so it never fires for Stream, which is known and merely hollow. The placeholder path cannot protect against a variant the build recognises but cannot fulfil.

So classify each path on two axes, not one:
1. Does the variant exist and decode?
2. When it cannot deliver, does it disclose that, or render a plausible
   in-progress state?

Every path failing (2) is a surface that lies during exactly the moment someone
is relying on it.

title: Enforce stream output contracts against a declared registry
description: StreamEnvelope.contract is the coupling point between producers, bindings and widget InputPorts, but nothing validates it. crates/canvas/src/stream_binding.rs checks only that the string is non-empty and 128 chars or fewer, so any producer can invent a contract name and any binding can reference one that does not exist. dock-cov.3's acceptance already calls for a registry that 'resolves exact authorized identities'; this is the concrete validation gap underneath it.
design: Three contracts exist today as bare string literals rather than a declared set: map.v1, market-ohlcv-v1 and widget-snapshot-v1. Two have binders on disk (binders/market-ohlcv-v1.lua, binders/widget-snapshot-v1.lua). Declare the contract set in one place and validate on both sides: a StreamEnvelope naming an unknown contract is rejected at ingress, and a DataBinding whose source contract does not match the target InputPort contract is rejected at apply time rather than silently delivering events a widget cannot read. Keep the check a lookup against declared contracts, not a hardcoded match, so adding a contract stays a data change. This is a one-way door: bindings persist inside saved workspace documents, so a contract name that ships wrong has to be migrated rather than renamed.
acceptance_criteria: An envelope naming an undeclared contract is refused at ingress with the contract named in the error. A binding whose source contract does not match its target InputPort contract is refused when applied, not at first event. Adding a contract requires no rebuild of the validation logic. Existing saved workspaces referencing the three current contracts still load.
notes: Found 2026-09-09 while mapping how Canvas defines available data streams. Path: producer -> stream.sock (owner-only Unix socket) -> StreamEnvelope{owner,stream,contract} -> binders/<adapter>.lua -> widget snapshot -> InputPort. The Lua binder layer is genuinely extensible already: apply_named_adapter loads binders/{adapter}.lua from disk, so a new adapter is a file drop with no rebuild. Contract naming is the one part of that path with no discipline, and it is the part that persists in saved documents.

title: Canvas: react to display reconfiguration and re-layout by display count
notes:
Canvas calls platform::displays() once at startup (crates/canvas/src/main.rs:362) and never re-enumerates. There is no CGDisplayRegisterReconfigurationCallback or equivalent observer anywhere in crates/canvas, canvas-core, or canvas-mac.

Two consequences, one root cause:

1. Enabling or disabling a monitor does not change the layout at all, which is
   the capability being asked for here.
2. If Canvas starts before Dock Control is running it enumerates displays=0 and
   renders nothing, permanently, until restarted. Observed 2026-09-09: Canvas
   reported visible=true with 22 surfaces and frame=120,100,1280,800 displays=0,
   and drew no window on any of three attached displays. Starting Dock Control
   first and relaunching gave frame=0,0,5760,1200 displays=3 and it rendered.

Shape:
- Detection belongs behind the existing canvas-core platform trait, so macOS
  registers a reconfiguration callback and Sway/other compositors implement the
  same narrow interface rather than each growing their own.
- On a change, re-enumerate, then re-materialize the active view against the new
  display set. operational_views::materialize already rebuilds placements from
  NormalizedRect, so the layout half largely exists; what is missing is the
  trigger and the per-display-count policy.
- Policy should be declared, not hardcoded: a mapping from display count to
  which view goes where, so patterns can be adjusted as they emerge without a
  rebuild. Intent stated by the owner: one display is focused on primary work;
  additional displays are operational. That is a natural fit for the existing
  saved operational views (fleet/runtime is a good operational candidate).
- Debounce. macOS emits several reconfiguration callbacks per change;
  re-materializing on each would thrash the layout.

Not yet decided: whether a manual layout a person has dragged should survive a
display change or be replaced by the policy layout. Worth deciding before
implementing, because it is the difference between a helpful and an infuriating
feature.
2026-09-09 root cause found for 'layout does not fit one monitor'.

self.frame is assigned in exactly one place (crates/canvas/src/main.rs:1895, on
display enumeration). apply_display_target sets selected_display_ids and calls
replace_host_windows(frames) but never updates self.frame.

fn view(&self, window) computes viewport_x = viewport.x - self.frame.x, so each
display window is a viewport into one large canvas spanning the union frame.
Normalized placements therefore map across the union, not per display. Toggling
to a single display with Ctrl-1 hides the other viewports rather than reflowing:
you see one third of the arrangement.

Two separable pieces:
- Fit: remap the current layout's normalized bounds into the active displays'
  sub-rect of the union frame. Computable from selected_display_frames() and
  self.frame, no new state. Safe as an explicit command.
- Automatic: make the canvas frame follow the selected displays so a display
  change reflows. This changes what Ctrl-1/2/3 mean today - they currently
  reveal and hide parts of a wide canvas rather than reflowing - so it should be
  a deliberate decision, not a side effect of adding fit.

Ctrl-Option-L (snap) is unaffected and correct: it restores the saved
arrangement faithfully. The arrangement is simply union-wide.

title: fpl-auth: device token introspection for workload services
description: fab (and later other services) must be able to verify a desktop device token and its scopes without holding a shared admin credential or reimplementing session logic. fpl-auth already stores desktop_bridges registrations with revocation; expose a narrow introspection endpoint for that.
design:
Narrow endpoint alongside the existing /credentials/desktop-bridge/resolve in
fpl-auth/src/main.rs. Input: device token. Output: owner identity, device id,
scopes, revocation state. Deny by default; a revoked device must fail closed and
promptly, since it gates binary downloads.

Do not hand fab a global admin token, and do not let a caller choose the
principal through a header or body field.
acceptance_criteria: fab can verify a device token and receive owner plus scopes; a revoked device fails immediately; the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate devices or impersonate a principal; revocation delay is measured and recorded.
notes:
2026-09-09 source review; the mechanism already exists, so this is a narrow addition rather than new machinery.

Reuse the credential-client pattern that /credentials/desktop-bridge/resolve
already uses (fpl-auth/src/main.rs:4008):
- Caller authenticates with Bearer <client secret>, matched by
  credential_client_for_secret (main.rs:9017), which is a constant-time compare
  against config.providers.credential_clients.
- CredentialClient is { id, secret, providers } (main.rs:462); authorization is
  an allowlist check on client.providers. fab gets its own client entry with a
  device-introspection provider; it never receives an admin token.

Device lookup: desktop_bridges (main.rs:5920) is keyed by device_id with a
UNIQUE index on token_hash, and carries email, display_name, platform_os,
platform_arch, route_url, capabilities, revoked_at. So introspection is a
token_hash lookup with a revoked_at IS NULL check; fail closed on revoked.

Scopes: access_for_email + can_use_scope are the existing grant model, already
used by resolve for its optional required_scope. Take the same optional
required_scope parameter rather than inventing a second scope vocabulary.

Deliberately NOT doing: no new token format, no per-device secret handed to
fab, no endpoint that lets a caller name the principal. The device token is the
only principal input, and it is proof by possession.

Open question for implementation: whether revocation needs to be faster than
fab's manifest cache. Record the measured revocation delay per the bead's
acceptance criteria.

title: fab: serve authenticated release channel manifests
description: Add the channel manifest and download-grant endpoint that 'fpl install' calls. fab already builds and publishes immutable artifacts to the fab-artifacts bucket with digests and a SigV4 signer; what is missing is a per-user authorized way to resolve 'current stable build of PRODUCT for TARGET' and hand back a short-lived URL.
design:
GET /v1/channels/{channel}/{product}/{target} in fab/crates/fabd/src/api.rs.
Verify the caller's device token against fpl-auth (see dock-cov.32) and check a
download scope. Reuse the manifest fields package-release.mjs already writes so
there is one artifact description, not two. Presigned URL lifetime in minutes.

Do not put artifact bytes behind fpl-auth: identity stays there, bytes stay in
fab. Channels start with 'stable'; the channel name is data, not a code path.
acceptance_criteria: A valid device token resolves a manifest and a working presigned URL for a published desktop release; a revoked or absent token is refused; an unknown product/target/channel is a clean 404; the presigned URL expires; no long-lived artifact credential is issued to a desktop.

title: fpl install: authenticated artifact download and setup
description: Add 'fpl install [PRODUCT...]' to the FPL CLI so one command sets up a machine's FPL binaries: fpl-desktop-bridge, canvas, and jarvis. Authenticates with the device credential written by 'fpl login', resolves a channel manifest, downloads, verifies sha256, and installs. Requires no bridge to already be present, since the bridge is one of the things it installs.
design:
Decided 2026-09-09: fab issues, fpl-auth authorizes.

GET {fab}/v1/channels/{channel}/{product}/{target}
  Authorization: Bearer <device token from the OS keyring>
  target is the Rust host triple (aarch64-apple-darwin), matching what
  desktop/fpl-desktop-bridge/scripts/package-release.mjs already emits.
Response reuses that script's existing manifest shape plus a short-lived
presigned URL: { version, tag, commit, target, artifact, sha256, size, url }.

fab already owns builds, the fab-artifacts bucket and a SigV4 signer
(fab/crates/fabd/src/artifact.rs), and already has a desktop release pipeline
(scripts/fab-release.mjs). fpl-auth stays the identity authority and does not
grow bucket credentials or serve binary traffic.

Client side lives in the FPL CLI next to src/login.rs and reads credentials
through the vendored fpl-enrollment crate. Verify sha256 before install; refuse
on mismatch rather than installing and warning.
acceptance_criteria: fpl install on a machine with only 'fpl login' completed installs a working fpl-desktop-bridge; sha256 is verified before install and a mismatch aborts; channel and version are reported; re-running is idempotent; a revoked device is refused by fab, not just by the CLI.

title: Adopt fpl login as the cross-platform bridge and workload enrollment path
description: Define the longer-term FPL CLI contract for one-time machine enrollment across Mac, Windows, Linux desktop, and Yggdrasil GPU boxes. fpl login should install/update required binaries, open SSO when a browser exists, support a pasted device code on headless machines, and provision scoped credentials into the MCP Bridge/OS secret store. Canvas and Jarvis consume the bridge; they do not implement independent login or copy browser cookies.
design: Reuse fpl-auth device authorization and credential-client patterns plus shared-infra fpl-desktop-bridge protocol. Keep Yggdrasil node enrollment distinct but compatible; avoid a global admin token and avoid duplicating auth in Canvas.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed contract names device identity, refresh/access token storage, scopes for Canvas/JARVIS/Prometheus, browser and headless flows, binary version/channel policy, revoke/rotate behavior, and offline/error states; Prometheus connector can authenticate through this owner without embedding secrets.
notes:
User direction 2026-09-09: consolidate into fpl CLI; fpl login on Mac Neo, Windows, Linux Canvas, and GPU/Yggdrasil boxes; browser SSO where available, paste code for headless; MCP Bridge likely common path, Canvas/Jarvis should remain clients.
2026-09-09 implemented (login half):

Decisions taken, both as recommended:
- Enrollment lives in a shared crate, shared-infra/desktop/fpl-enrollment,
  vendored into engineering-tenets/vendor/fpl-enrollment with SHA-256
  provenance. This breaks the bootstrap cycle: fpl login must enroll a machine
  before fpl-desktop-bridge exists on it, because the credential authorizes
  downloading the bridge.
- Artifacts: fab issues manifests and presigned URLs, fpl-auth authorizes.
  Tracked as dock-cov.31/.32/.33.

Landed on shared-infra branch feat/fpl-login-enrollment:
- fpl-enrollment crate: identity, pairing, keyring slots, whoami, sign-out,

- fpl-desktop-bridge migrated onto it (-244 lines); 89 tests pass and the iced
  desktop feature still builds. Pairing::device_code is now private, so the
  bridge can no longer read the polling proof.

In engineering-tenets working tree (NOT committed; see below):
- fpl login / whoami / logout, --no-browser, --json, --force, idempotent re-run.
- vendor provenance test.

Boundary confirmed with the user: Canvas and JARVIS must NOT link the crate.
Linking it grants the ability to read the device token from the keyring, which
is the ad-hoc credential Canvas is meant to avoid. Rule of thumb: link the crate
only if you must work before the bridge exists. Everything else is a client of
the running bridge.

Installed state deliberately unchanged: keyring service dev.fpl.desktop-bridge,
accounts <device-id> and <device-id>:session, the FPL Desktop Bridge state dir,
and FPL_DESKTOP_BRIDGE_CONFIG. identity.json is a new sibling of config.json;
a machine already enrolled by the bridge is adopted, and config.json is never
rewritten. Verified against this Mac's real config (mac-studio).

Verified against real sso.fpl.dev: begin succeeds, approval-origin check passes,
headless flow prints a usable URL, neither output path leaks device_code.
NOT verified: post-approval poll, which needs a human to click approve.

Blocked: engineering-tenets could not be committed. Its master has pre-existing

title: Connect Prometheus owners to Canvas snapshot streams
description: Implement the owner-side Prometheus transport required by operational views. Resolve stable connector/query identities to authenticated instant/range queries, emit canvas.widget.snapshot.v1 envelopes to Canvas stream.sock, and report reconnect, unauthorized, no-data, stale, and source-error states with observed timestamps. Keep credentials/endpoints out of view JSON and Lua; Lua remains a bounded typed adapter.
acceptance_criteria: bifrost/runtime and elmers/now leave Loading with deterministic fixture-backed Prometheus events; real transport has bounded cadence/backpressure and reconnect behavior; unauthorized/no-data/stale/error states are visible; tests cover query normalization and emitted snapshot envelopes.
notes:
Readiness audit 2026-09-09: config/views/*.json declare prometheus:* sources and Canvas materialization maps them to owner streams, but this repository contains no Prometheus HTTP/query owner or emitter. stream_binding.rs only receives Unix datagrams and applies events already present in the inbox. Therefore widgets remain Loading by design until an owner emits canvas.widget.snapshot.v1.
Endpoint probe 2026-09-09: https://prometheus.fpl.dev/ and standard /api/v1/query?query=up both return Cloudflare HTTP 404 route not found without authentication. Before implementing a client, verify the canonical Prometheus API base path and whether SSO is browser-only or a service credential/OIDC client grant is available. Do not bake an assumed path or token flow into Canvas.
Endpoint clarification 2026-09-09: user supplied https://prom.fpl.dev/query. Probes show prom.fpl.dev/query, /api/v1/query?query=up, and /-/ready all HTTP 302 to sso.fpl.dev/login, confirming the host is SSO-gated rather than absent. Implement against Prometheus-compatible /api/v1/query and /api/v1/query_range once an owner-side service credential/OIDC exchange is identified; browser cookies must not be copied into Canvas.
Auth design alignment: reuse fpl-auth/Desktop MCP Bridge identity model rather than Canvas-owned login. fpl-auth cli-access-model.md defines device approval, scoped workload credentials, and no browser-cookie handoff; shared-infra desktop-bridge/protocol.md defines per-device refresh credential in OS secret store and short-lived access tokens. Preferred path: fpl login performs browser/device-code enrollment, installs/updates fpl-desktop-bridge, and Prometheus owner uses a scoped bridge/service credential to query prom.fpl.dev. Canvas receives only normalized snapshots over the local bridge/socket.
2026-09-09 blocking analysis corrected by source review.

Earlier notes said Prometheus waits on a service-credential exchange. Reading
the actual path shows the credential this needs already exists once a machine
completes fpl login; it is NOT blocked on the artifact/download work
(dock-cov.31/.32/.33), which concerns binary distribution only.

The chain, verified by reading source:
- desktop_pairing::approve inserts a real fpl-auth session for the returned
  session_token, carrying the approving browser session's own scopes
  (fpl-auth/src/desktop_pairing.rs, insert_session with &session.scopes).
- fpl login stores that session_token in the OS keyring
  (<device-id>:session).
- Palisade forwards the Authorization header to fpl-auth when vouching
  (palisade/src/auth.rs:244).
- fpl-auth /vouch accepts a bearer token as a cookie fallback, hashes it and
  resolves it as a session (fpl-auth/src/main.rs:4904), then applies the
  route's required scope.

So an owner process can call prom.fpl.dev /api/v1/query with
Authorization: Bearer <session token> and be vouched, provided the owner's
grants include the scope that route requires. No browser cookie is copied.

NOT yet verified empirically: no approved session exists on this machine, so
this is a code-read conclusion, not an observed 200. Next step is one browser
approval of fpl login, then probe /api/v1/query?query=up with that bearer
before writing the owner.

Known constraint to design for: the paired session expires with the approving
SSO session, so a long-running Prometheus owner needs a re-auth path rather
than assuming an indefinitely valid token. That, not initial auth, is the real
open question for this bead.
2026-09-09 credential path implemented and verified live.

Decision: bridge egress proxy. Canvas connectors never hold the owner's bearer;
the bridge attaches it. Implemented as metric_reads in fpl-desktop-bridge,
modelled on the existing project_reads precedent rather than a new mechanism.

Shape: caller names an operation plus PromQL over the owner-only IPC socket
(0600 in a 0700 dir, peer uid checked). No arbitrary-path passthrough - the
route table allows only /api/v1/query, /api/v1/query_range and /-/ready,
because a caller that could choose the path could reach anything the owner's
session can reach. PromQL is percent-encoded so a query cannot append
parameters. Metrics base URL is desktop.metricsBaseUrl, default
https://prom.fpl.dev, validated through the enrollment endpoint rule.

Verified live on Mac Studio after installing and restarting the LaunchAgent:
- metric-read query 'up' returns real series
- metric-read query_range with 1800s/60s returns 17 points for job=bifrost
- metric-read ready returns 'Prometheus Server is Ready.'
- out-of-bounds ranges and unknown operations are refused through the live path
- no credential appears in any output
Bridge health after restart shows state running with connectors serving.

Remaining for this bead: the Canvas-side connector that turns these results
into canvas.widget.snapshot.v1 envelopes on stream.sock (owner=bifrost,
stream=prometheus-<name>, contract=canvas.widget.snapshot.v1), a mapping from
logical widget source ids (bifrost/health, bifrost/queue, ...) to PromQL, and
re-auth on authorization_denied which should auto-open the browser. The
snapshot payload shape is fixed by the widget-snapshot-v1 adapter test in
crates/canvas/src/stream_binding.rs.

title: Keep curated executive views fresh and visibly trustworthy
description: Add the freshness/reconciliation path for Alfalfa-curated Canvas views. Revalidate source/query revisions and connector health on refresh, preserve the last known-good composition, and surface stale/partial/disconnected/error states with observed-at and policy context. Never silently present old operational data as current.
acceptance_criteria: Every live widget exposes source and observed-at/freshness state; stale or drifted sources produce deterministic visible status and a receipt; refresh is bounded and idempotent; last-known-good layout remains usable while data degrades; tests cover source timeout, schema drift, partial inputs, recovery and restart.
notes: Partner freshness work follows alfalfa-i86w recommendation revisions. Preserve last-known-good layout while exposing source health and observed-at; no silent stale-as-current display.

title: Define Alfalfa-to-Canvas executive-view recommendation contract
description: Define the narrow versioned boundary between Alfalfa recommendations and Canvas operational views. Carry project/view identity, rationale, audience/privacy policy, stable connector/query IDs, bounded widget/layout intent, theme reference, refresh/freshness policy, evidence revision and acceptance/provenance receipts. Keep it proposal-only and revision-checked.
acceptance_criteria: A validated JSON/MCP contract round-trips with stable IDs and explicit bounds; invalid/unknown widgets, sources, privacy classes, stale evidence and conflicting revisions fail visibly; credentials/endpoints/raw payloads are excluded; an accepted recommendation can map to an existing named view without duplicating Canvas workspace or source ownership.
notes: Partner contract work should align with alfalfa-i86w.1 and dock-cov.29.2. Recommendation is proposal-only, revision-checked and capability-validated.

title: Let Alfalfa curate fresh executive views per project
description: Use Alfalfa-owned project/resource identity and operational evidence to recommend an initial executive Canvas view for each project, then keep the selected composition fresh over time. Alfalfa decides/curates the view intent and priority; Canvas materializes the named view with widgets, layout, theme, provenance, freshness and explicit degraded states. Never copy credentials, endpoints, private source payloads, or domain mutation logic into Canvas.
design: Alfalfa owns project catalog, evidence, recommendation policy and revision history. Source systems own metrics and mutations. Canvas owns deterministic rendering, widget bounds, theme/presentation and freshness display. Recommendations are proposals, not arbitrary executable UI: validate against a Canvas capability catalog, require stable connector/query IDs, cap widgets and cadence, and preserve the last known-good view while surfacing staleness. Use an explicit accept/promote receipt; do not let an LLM directly rewrite workspace documents.
acceptance_criteria: For each enrolled project, Alfalfa can return a versioned executive-view recommendation with rationale, source/query identities, audience/privacy policy, refresh/freshness policy, and a bounded widget/layout proposal. Canvas can preview and accept the recommendation through an owner-authorized contract, materialize it using existing operational-view documents, and show source health/freshness. Refresh or source drift produces a visible revision/receipt; stale data never silently appears current; human and agent can inspect the exact active view and provenance. Initial packs include bifrost/runtime and elmers/now, with measured extension points for Auth, Lab, JARVIS, and Panopticon.
notes:
Cross-project partner: alfalfa-i86w with child alfalfa-i86w.1. Coherence direction: executive surface should lead with one decision-useful hero signal, keep supporting KPIs compact, use project theme tokens and shared WidgetFrame/plot recipes, disclose source + observed-at/freshness near every live signal, and reserve motion for state/change communication. Alfalfa recommends; Canvas validates/materializes; sources own metrics and mutations. Preserve last-known-good composition while making stale/partial/error states unmistakable.
User clarified this belongs in the larger Alfalfa onboarding flow. Treat dock-cov.29 as the Canvas half of onboarding: consume the accepted recommendation after Alfalfa verifies scope, ownership, outcomes, resources and evidence; do not invent an independent Canvas dashboard planner.

title: Add theme picker and bounded presentation effects
description: Canvas owns the general theme and animation improvement cut. Add an F2-background-picker-style keyboard palette/theme selector, plus the bounded attention-effect catalog transferred from Jarvis issue jarvis-e96.2: gentle pulse, directional highlight, progress sweep, arrival accent, completion accent and urgent alert. Effects are named capabilities, never arbitrary animation code or raw audio, and remain independent from report content and narration.
design: Reuse the existing Canvas transition clock and Coherence-derived theme source. Keep ThemeSelection as the persisted source of truth; the picker previews and commits declared light/dark/accent combinations without duplicating palettes. Define versioned effect IDs with bounded parameters, duration, intensity, repeat/rate limits, interruption, reduced-motion policy and cancellation. Canvas renders effects and returns explicit receipts; Jarvis/Subconscious may choose urgency but cannot inject shaders, code, files or audio. Keep explanatory/timeline animation in dock-cov.25.
acceptance_criteria: A keyboard shortcut opens a visual theme/palette selector analogous to F2 backgrounds; navigation previews Coherence light/dark/accent choices, Enter persists the selection, Escape restores the prior selection, and tests cover event routing and persistence. A versioned effect catalog is capability-negotiated, GPU-bounded, cancellable and rate-limited; effects synchronize to presentation steps; reduced-motion and muted-audio modes work; unsupported effects degrade to a quiet highlight with an explicit receipt; urgent cues cannot become an unbounded alarm.
notes: 2026-09-08 first slice: implemented F4 visual theme picker for Coherence light/dark × brand/info/success, whole-Canvas live preview, Escape restore, Enter workspace-local persistence via explicit ThemeRef selection, shortcut help and schema support. Focused picker, routing, persistence and canvas-core tests pass; MCP schema check passes; cargo build --workspace passes. Full cargo test --workspace could not link after local disk hit ENOSPC; external-volume retry was interrupted by a concurrently removed Cargo registry web-time source. Effect catalog/rendering/receipts/reduced-motion remain next.

title: Show active workspace with a themed FPL vector mark
description: Replace Canvas's plain-text bottom-left FPL badge with the canonical path-based FPL SVG and a quiet active-workspace identity. The mark must render only on the configured leftmost overlay display, derive its frosted surface and foreground from the active workspace Coherence palette, update immediately when the project workspace changes, and avoid becoming a dock or persistent toolbar.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas embeds the canonical path-only FPL vector asset; the bottom-left identity shows the project display name with project-id fallback; colors derive from the active workspace palette in light and dark themes; existing overlay targeting remains configurable; tests cover identity resolution and the workspace tests/build/clippy pass; the installed Canvas is visually verified.

title: Avoid macOS-reserved workspace cycling shortcuts
description: Canvas currently binds Control+Up/Down for project workspace cycling, but macOS consumes those chords for Mission Control and App Exposé before the focused Canvas desktop receives them. Move cycling to an available chord while preserving the workspace command and MCP interface.
design: Use Control+Shift+Up/Down in the focused Canvas desktop. This keeps the directional model and avoids the enabled macOS Control+Arrow symbolic hotkeys. Match the full modifier set so plain Control+Arrow remains available to macOS and terminal applications. Update the visible help and focused tests.
acceptance_criteria: Control+Shift+Up/Down cycle previous/next project workspaces when Canvas desktop input is focused; Control+Up/Down do not trigger Canvas switching; extra Option or Command modifiers do not match; help displays the actual chord; focused unit tests pass.
notes: Implemented Control+Shift+Up/Down matching with exact modifier rejection, updated the focused help overlay, and added a regression test proving plain Control+Arrow and extra Option do not match. While validating, repaired the in-flight background picker library/binary ownership boundary and deterministic speed tie behavior. Validation: canvas lib 106/106; canvas GUI 50/50; strict canvas binary Clippy passed. Installed matching GUI/MCP binaries. Live macOS synthetic-key proof switched dock -> bifrost with Control+Shift+Up and restored bifrost -> dock with Control+Shift+Down; owner store and control socket remain mode 0600.

title: Author source-backed named operational view packs
description: Turn the audited operational questions into project-scoped named Canvas view presets, beginning with bifrost/runtime and elmers/now, then Auth, Invoker, Lab, JARVIS and Panopticon. This bead covers widget composition, source/query references, layout, theme and freshness policy only; it does not change workspace switching or MCP activation contracts.
design: Use docs/audits/canvas-operational-view-inventory.json as a non-runtime proposal and promote entries individually into the existing validated view format. Presets contain stable connector/query identities and layout, never endpoints, credentials, or copied secrets. Keep mutation workflows in owner applications through deep links. Run Canvas beside Grafana until parity is demonstrated.

title: Build Canvas notifications with JARVIS announcement handoff
description: Create a coherent notification surface for incoming operational alerts, messages, reminders, and source events. Canvas owns visual delivery, bounded history, unread/announced presentation, grouping, and deep links. JARVIS owns announcement policy and speech; source owners own acknowledgement and mutations.
design: Normalize notifications into a typed envelope with stable id, source, severity, timestamp, title/body, optional subject/entity, dedupe key, expiry, privacy class, and owner deep link. Support transient toast/rail plus a notification-center view. Delivery and announcement receipts prevent repeats across reconnects; no source payload is spoken unless policy marks it announceable.

title: Audit FPL operational UIs for Canvas saved views
description: Inventory current operational dashboards, read-only UI surfaces, Prometheus/Grafana panels, and Canvas widget coverage. Define named project-scoped view presets, reusable widget gaps, connector needs, and a Coherence visual-quality rubric. Keep workspace switching and activation contracts out of scope.

title: Reduce idle Canvas CPU and redraw work
description: Canvas native rendering is GPU-backed through wgpu/Metal, but a 5 Hz candle feed still measured roughly 27-33% of one CPU core. Profile background, iced layout, command preparation, and redraw invalidation; redraw only surfaces affected by retained-state changes and preserve current bounded stream latency.
acceptance_criteria: On the three-monitor ops workspace, measure and document idle and 5 Hz CPU before/after; reduce unnecessary full-desktop redraw work without regressing animation cadence, event age, input handling, or visual output.

title: Bind native widgets to bounded realtime streams
description: Canvas widgets declare typed stream bindings. A host-owned connector subscribes to local JSONL/SSE-style events, validates and bounds them, folds them into retained widget state, and requests redraw. The socket and MCP select intent/source/view; they do not push presentation frames or repeated widget replacements.
design: Host connector owns I/O, credentials, reconnection, ordering, rate limiting, and bounded event delivery. Sandboxed Lua receives one immutable event plus declared context and returns one known WidgetMutation. canvas-widgets validates/applies the mutation with history bounds. Renderers remain pure. Binding identity belongs to workspace DataBinding.
acceptance_criteria: A running quant-candles widget binds to a named local stream, receives repeated validated OHLCV events without reopening the surface, retains its identity/layout/focus, visibly redraws, bounds history, and fails invalid events loudly. Tests cover reducer behavior, bounds, and malformed events.
notes: Delivery must be latency-aware. Persist per-binding policy: latest/coalesced for gauges/presence/current price; ordered bounded batches for candles/events/graph firing. Envelopes include monotonic source sequence and emitted timestamp. Track queue depth, dropped/coalesced events and end-to-end age. For OHLCV, completed candles remain ordered while same-timestamp updates to the forming candle replace/coalesce. Lua executes per bounded batch, never per render frame.
close_reason: Implemented owner-local bounded stream ingress, durable latency-aware bindings, sandboxed Lua batch adapters, atomic typed candle mutations, and verified live native redraw at 5 Hz plus a 500 Hz stress burst.

title: Make quant surfaces theme-native and snap-resizable
description: The candlestick preview exposed the distinction between file/image surfaces and native widgets. Ship the quant renderer in the live Canvas binary, verify its Coherence palette is resolved per workspace, ensure it fills arbitrary widget bounds without intrinsic aspect locking, and verify move/resize snapping uses the shared interaction path.
design: Keep quant presentation in canvas-widgets::live::quant. Do not add chart-specific window movement logic; reuse normalized surface bounds and shared interaction snapping.
acceptance_criteria: A quant candlestick opened through open_widget inherits the active workspace VisualTheme, fills and reflows across tested wide/tall bounds, and move/resize snaps exactly like other widget surfaces. The PNG preview is removed after live replacement.
notes: Removed the misleading PNG preview and temporary artifact. Native quant renderer now derives every color from VisualTheme and computes a responsive ChartLayout from current bounds; added wide/tall and volume-hidden layout tests. Live build is blocked at OS process launch: freshly linked Mach-O binaries hang before dyld/main, syspolicyd PID 4879 is in uninterruptible state, and noninteractive sudo cannot restart it. Do not reopen a preview; completion requires real open_widget acceptance in installed binary.
close_reason: Installed the native Canvas binary, opened quant-candles through open_widget, and verified the live surface reports content=widget with no raster asset or intrinsic pixel dimensions. Renderer derives Coherence VisualTheme colors, reflows from allocated bounds, and shares the normal placement/interaction path. Agora validation passed 18 tests and strict Clippy.

title: Add a modular quant widget kit with native candlesticks
description: Establish a kit boundary inside canvas-widgets and add a first typed trading visualization: bounded OHLCV candlesticks with volume, native iced rendering, Coherence theme roles, and durable JSON/MCP schema.

This keeps domain schemas and renderers modular while preserving one durable WidgetSpec. Lua remains the extension path for compositions that map to existing primitives; new GPU/native primitives enter through focused kits. Candle timestamps must be strictly increasing; OHLC and volume are finite and internally consistent; rendering is retained and bounded.

title: Toggle the Canvas diagnostics HUD with F3
description: Add the classic F3 diagnostics toggle so the passive conky-style local metrics HUD can be shown or hidden without editing workspace layout.
design: Handle an unmodified non-repeating F3 keyboard event inside Canvas. Visibility is transient runtime UI state, independent of project workspace persistence and the configured screen anchor.

title: Carry first Coherence visual slice through Canvas widgets
description: Expand the native theme boundary with a compact, typed set of surface, typography, geometry, interaction, and data-viz concepts. Apply the resolved project theme across every dock-widget family and preserve deterministic workspace/project switching.
design: Keep the contract narrow: VisualTheme resolves palette plus semantic metrics/recipes from the project ThemeSelection. Widgets consume the whole VisualTheme, never individual ad-hoc constants. Coherence remains the upstream token owner; this cut uses generated vendored tokens and creates a stable consumer boundary that coherence-iced can own without changing widget APIs.
acceptance_criteria: All current live widget kinds consume shared theme typography, spacing, radii, surface alpha, borders, chart colors, and status colors; no literal RGB status colors remain; workspace project theme resolution changes the full widget treatment; dark and light theme tests cover the resolved contracts; workspace build, tests, fmt, and clippy pass.
notes: First deliberately narrow vertical slice under dock-cov.15.
close_reason: Resolved project themes now carry semantic surface, typography, geometry, opacity, elevation, focus, and data-viz roles through every live widget; imported palettes share the same path; workspace tests, strict clippy, build, and live app install passed.

title: Make Coherence the native Canvas style owner
description: Canvas currently consumes a reduced Coherence color palette but hardcodes most iced component recipes: typography sizes, spacing, radii, opacity, elevation, window chrome, instrument panels, tables, charts, meters, focus and hover. Promote the native renderer boundary so Coherence owns semantic visual tokens and reusable iced style/component functions while Canvas owns layout, data, interaction, and workspace state.
design: Do not parse browser CSS inside iced and do not introduce a general styling language. Keep Coherence's current CSS custom properties as the canonical token source; extend its bounded exporter to generate complete Rust tokens. Define a small shared component contract—role, variant, interaction state, density and size class—with CSS and coherence-iced implementations both owned and parity-tested in Coherence. Theme data remains project-scoped and serializable; Lua receives read-only semantic tokens and selects declared variants but cannot invent ambient styling or own rendering. Commit Coherence first, then sync a pinned checksummed snapshot into Dock; do not copy component recipes into Dock.
acceptance_criteria: A committed and versioned coherence-iced artifact is synced into Dock with provenance; Dock no longer projects Coherence into a lossy color-only ThemePalette for native components; semantic typography, full spacing/radius/density, surface layers, focus, opacity/elevation and data-viz roles reach iced; Canvas chrome and dock-widgets use shared Coherence recipes; light/dark/project/imported palette modes render legibly; visual fixtures and keyboard focus states are verified; consumer sync detects drift.
notes:
Audit 2026-09-08: Dock's vendored coherence-tokens snapshot exposes upstream colors/spacing/radii but ThemePalette keeps only 13 colors and ThemeMetrics keeps four spaces, one radius and two font sizes. dock-widgets::live accepts only ThemePalette and hardcodes panel padding 16, radius 7, alpha 0.72, type sizes, shadow and graph treatments; Canvas independently hardcodes chrome/dock/HUD styles. Local Coherence has an uncommitted coherence-iced draft with theme/button/input/select/divider/action/account-row functions and richer Precise tokens. Preserve that work, commit it upstream, add Canvas/data-viz recipes there, then sync through scripts/sync-components.mjs with provenance.
Operational-view visual rubric is recorded in docs/audits/canvas-operational-view-audit.md. Coherence needs semantic data-series roles, compact/comfortable density, tabular number treatment, plot grid/axis/annotation roles, explicit data-health states, and a shared WidgetFrame/PlotFrame recipe across every widget.

title: Add display toggles and screen-aware surface placement
description: Canvas needs deterministic left/center/right display control for humans and agents. Add Ctrl-1/Ctrl-2/Ctrl-3 to toggle individual displays, Ctrl-0 to show Canvas on all displays, ordinal display targeting over MCP/socket, and a placement helper that can put a surface in a named region of a chosen display while preserving work on other screens.
design: Keep display topology and region-to-normalized-layout conversion in dock-canvas. MCP expresses intent using one-based display ordinals and stable surface IDs; the owner-local runtime resolves current geometry and emits exact state transitions. Preserve unrelated surface placements and expose resulting state in receipts/inspection.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl-0 through Ctrl-3 operate on displays ordered left-to-right; non-contiguous selections such as displays 1 and 3 work; MCP exposes ordinal display selection and exact display geometry; an agent can place one surface on the left while preserving an ops view on the right; commands are deterministic, revision-aware, validated, and covered by tests.

Live proof placed computing-mesh-design.md on display 1 while the six-surface ops board stayed on display 3; middle display remained normal macOS. Focused tests and strict Clippy pass.

title: Build the Canvas operational widget primitive suite
description: Create high-quality native Canvas building blocks for Prometheus/Grafana-style read-only operational views. Cover the useful vocabulary rather than copying Grafana screens: stat/value, time series, gauge, bar gauge/VU, status/alert, table, histogram/heatmap, logs/events, and node/DAG summaries. Every primitive consumes bounded typed data and Coherence semantic palette roles, supports dark/light/project themes, and composes into a saved widget board.
design: Use a dense instrument-panel language: deep semantic surfaces, hairline borders, left-aligned labels/values, readable units and freshness, reserved success/warning/danger state, and motion only for meaningful live changes. Keep the renderer native iced/wgpu. Add per-surface chrome mode so operational widgets can use a quiet draggable strip without close/minimize/maximize dots while retaining move/resize semantics. Connector I/O remains outside widget renderers.
acceptance_criteria: Native production renderers exist for stat, time series, gauge, bar/VU meter, status/alert, table, histogram/heatmap, event/log, and node summary specs; malformed or unbounded data fails validation; all colors derive from ThemePalette; dark and light fixtures render legibly; a surface can select standard or drag-only chrome and hit testing matches visible controls; a representative ops board is live-tested and visually reviewed.

2026-09-09: All current operational primitive families accept a generic validated snapshot mutation without exposing layout/theme/chrome to stream data. Full workspace tests pass; live stat snapshot rendered through the deployed Lua binder.
Readiness audit 2026-09-09: generic snapshot + Lua binder and explicit data-state labels are tested, but full-family visual legibility is not. See child dock-cov.8.3.1 for fixture/renderer verification; audit lists missing shared frame, axes, distribution/table/event details and chart placeholder.

title: Prove operational views with Prometheus and owner SSE connectors
description: Implement initial read-only connector adapters using the dock-cov.3 contract: Prometheus instant/range queries and authenticated ordered SSE feeds from Elmer's or MCP Bridge. Feed their typed outputs into retained Lua/widget scenes so Canvas can render gauges, time series, firing graphs, and DAG activity without a separate Grafana or source-specific UI. Ship a project-scoped saved operational-view fixture that JARVIS can later activate by exact project/view identity.
